results.strategy_description:
MY Asian Opportunities Fund invests primarily in the securities of Asian companies using a catalyst-driven, fundamental value approach. The Fund targets event-driven situations with asymmetric return profiles, including M&A, corporate restructurings, distressed opportunities, and arbitrage opportunities created by market dislocation.

We target investments with the potential for transformative change and where we believe there is an asymmetric return profile: 
1.	Special Situations: Opportunities as a result of increasing corporate activity through spin-offs, asset sales, divestitures, and stock buybacks
2.	Arbitrage: Opportunities as companies seek growth or to increase value via mergers and acquisitions
3.	Credit: Opportunities in bankruptcies, restructurings, refinancing, M&A, convertible bonds and credit default swaps

Additionally, the Special Investments Class was established with the purpose of allowing investors to participate in certain private assets, while not impacting the liquidity of the Fund. Investors can Opt-In on a monthly basis and Opt-Out annually on July 1 with 60-day notice. Private assets examples include pre-IPO positions, distressed debt and private investments in public equity, among others. At the time of investment, the aggregate amount of the Special Investments Class will not exceed 15% of eligible interests in the Fund.

results.management_company_description:
LMR Partners was set up in November 2009 by the founding partners, Ben Levine, Stefan Renold and Andrew Manuel.
The flagship Fund, the LMR Master Fund Limited, was launched on 1st February 2010 and runs a global, liquid, multi-asset investment strategy, employing both systematic and discretionary sub-strategies across asset classes.

Our investment philosophy is to exploit relative value opportunities across a range of asset classes, regions and time horizons.
We aim to build a diversified investment portfolio with a low correlation between separate strategies and strive to achieve absolute returns with a low correlation to markets.

Firm assets under management are approximately $10.7bn (as at 30th August 2023).
There are currently 260 employees Firm-wide, across London, Hong Kong, New York, Zurich, Dubai And Glasgow, with 110 investment professionals and 150 non-investment professionals (as at 30th August 2023).
results.strategy_description:
The CCSA strategy has been managed within the flagship Multi-Strategy Fund (the LMR Multi-Strategy Fund) since November 2018. The CCSA strategy
continues to be traded within the LMR Multi-Strategy Fund, pari passu to the LMR CCSA Fund. The LMR CCSA Fund employs a global convertible and capital structure arbitrage strategy that seeks to target returns on a predefined time horizon through fair value convergence and asymmetric implementation of catalyst driven trades. The Fund aims to achieve consistent risk-adjusted returns for its investors, in a market agnostic fashion.

results.strategy_description:
We deploy capital across a diverse selection of mostly market neutral investment strategies spanning a variety of asset classes, regions and horizons. 
We aim to balance capital across sub-strategies focused on exploiting inefficiencies within fixed income, equity, credit, volatility, equity arbitrate & event, and commodities driven markets. Each of these product lines / asset classes are overseen by a dedicated Product Head.
Each sub-strategy within the Fund is run by an expert portfolio manager or trading team, with each group working independently, effecting investments for their own segregated investment portfolio. 
Trading teams managing separate sub-strategies may be led by one or more portfolio managers. Teams with multiple portfolio managers may work collaboratively on investments for such portfolio. Such collaborative teams and their portfolios are however functionally segregated from other portfolio managers / trading teams.
All portfolio managers / trading teams are overseen by a formal Risk Committee comprised of Product Heads, the Chief Operating Officer, and Chief Risk Officer.
As a result of the segregation of portfolio managers / trading teams and as an inherent facet of our multi-strategy approach, such teams may take opposing positions in the same investments / securities, notwithstanding that such trading positions have been affected for the same fund.

results.strategy_description:
Wellington Global Technology Long/Short Fund is a technology hedge fund managed by Bruce Glazer. The fund combines experienced technology investors in a proven investment process that is grounded in bottom-up fundamental research. The fund was launched in January 2000.

The portfolio manager looks for investments across the spectrum of global technology companies, with a focus on those subsectors and companies that are likely to generate attractive absolute returns while also leveraging the research produced by other Wellington Management technology analysts.

The investment process is based on bottom-up, fundamental analysis of technology companies worldwide. The portfolio is continually rebalanced so that investments are made in those sectors and companies that are most appealing at any time. As a result, exposure to individual sub-sectors within technology will depend on supply-demand characteristics, secular trends, existing product evaluations, and new product developments. Focus is on direct contact with company management, suppliers, and competitors to identify favorable investment opportunities not yet recognized by the market. The key objective of the partnership is to achieve superior total returns on an absolute basis. In order to achieve this goal, the manager invests in companies with growth potential and good stock appreciation potential, while taking short positions in poorly positioned companies with unsustainable valuations.

It is diversified across sectors and regions, with an emphasis on TMT/Consumer (50-60% exposure) in the US (50-75% exposure). Tracing its origins to 1928, Wellington Management’s exclusive focus is the management of client portfolios for retirement plans, endowments and foundations, public funds, mutual fund sponsors, insurance companies, governments and supranationals, private investment funds, and high net worth investors worldwide. Wellington Management serves as investment manager or sub-adviser to each of the funds sponsored by Wellington Alternative Investments (WAI).

Wellington Management Group LLP, the parent company of our global organization, is a private partnership with 1921 partners, all active in the business, and 976 investment professionals. We serve our global client base from 17 offices located worldwide. Our most distinctive strength is our proprietary, independent research, which is shared across all areas of the organization as part of our collaborative approach to investing and used only for managing our clients’ portfolios. The separation of business functions from investment functions at Wellington Management allows our investment professionals to focus exclusively on the management of client portfolios and creates natural checks and balances throughout the investment process.

Market cap is unconstrained, typically >US $500 million, at the time of purchase, while country and sector weights are unconstrained, and result of bottom-up stock selection.

Factor exposures are unconstrained, however these are monitored carefully and expected to vary over time. Robust, risk management processes and tools are in place to limit any unintended factor exposures, including the use of index options.

results.strategy_description:
Bay Pond:
Bay Pond is an opportunistic long/short equity approach with a focus on financials and fintech and a track record dating back to 1994. Bay Pond is managed by Nick Adams, who leads (along with Matt Lipton) a six-person dedicated portfolio management team with over 100 years of combined professional experience, and is supported by an 11-member global finance research team and the broader resources of Wellington Management Company. Investing successfully across the financial services sector requires both specialization and a deep network of relationships cultivated over years of interactions. At Wellington, we believe our edge in is in the proprietary data we collect, our specialist focus, and our decades of relationships in the sector.

Investment Approach: 
Bay Pond seeks capital appreciation by investing in both long and short positions primarily in the financial services and related sectors. The portfolio invests primarily in banks, insurance companies, asset managers, broker dealers, mortgage banks, commercial and consumer finance firms, REITs, and financial technology companies. Bay Pond is typically directional but dynamically hedged to protect capital in down markets.

Our investment framework focuses on deep, bottom-up, fundamental research, through which we look up and down the capital structure and across sub-sectors and geographies. The impact of disruptive technologies, interest rate levels, yield curve shape, credit markets, regulation, and the health of the economy is embedded in our investment lens. The approach does not require a directional view on financial stocks, just an appreciation that high volatility and meaningful dispersion within the sector will offer attractive investment opportunities across this diverse and nuanced sector. We utilize a wide range of hedging techniques to potentially enhance returns, mitigate risk, and protect capital.

results.strategy_description:
Global Research Equity Extended is a long/short equity fund that seeks to outperform the MSCI World (Net) Index consistently over market cycles through stock selection by a team of experienced industry-focused sub-portfolio managers. Each sub-portfolio manager is responsible for a sleeve of the fund, investing within their industries of expertise. The fund will aim to maintain a net exposure of 100%. In contrast to traditional long-only equity funds, gross leverage provides each sub-portfolio manager with additional flexibility to overweight and underweight stocks versus the benchmark. With capital allocated across a diverse set of industries and managed by sub-portfolio managers with differentiated investment styles, the fund aims to maintain high active share with a moderate and balanced risk profile versus the benchmark. Allocation of capital across the sleeves and the overall risk profile of the fund are managed by the Fundamental Factor Platform team.
The fund consists of multiple industry-based sleeves managed by a team of sub-portfolio managers, and each sleeve will hold long and short positions in individual equity securities while seeking to maintain a net exposure of approximately 100%. The fund is expected to have sector exposures which are typically similar to the MSCI World (Net) Index, a gross exposure between approximately 200-250%, a net exposure of approximately 100%, and a beta close to 1.0. In addition, exposures to risk factors for the fund will be managed by Edward Baldini and John Smallcomb, who are members of the Fundamental Factor Platform team, through capital allocation, gross leverage allocation, and risk-based hedges.

Each sub-portfolio manager is responsible for a sleeve of the fund, investing within their industries of expertise. The fund will aim to maintain a net exposure of 100%. In addition, exposures to risk factors for the fund will be managed by Edward Baldini and John Smallcomb who are members of the Fundamental Factor Platform team, through capital allocation, gross leverage allocation, and risk-based hedges.

results.strategy_description:
Fund Summary:
The Fund's objective is to generate consistent alpha, independent from market beta and risk assets through time, by combining specialization, diversification, and risk management. The process combines the discipline of fundamental macro research with independent risk-taking. The investment opportunity set consists primarily of fixed income (both rates and credit), currency and equity markets.
Investment Approach:
The investment process has three key components: idea generation, capital allocation, and risk management.
Investment ideas are generated based on an objective and risk-managed macro research process designed to identify structural imbalances, turning points in the business cycle and implications for the macro policy environment. Macro research is a specialized process purely focused on idea generation and is independent of market risk-taking. This separation enables the minimization of behavioral biases in interpreting macro data and allows for timely shifts in the macroeconomic outlook. The focus of the global bond strategists is to identify the macro scenarios that are most likely to occur. The identification of key guideposts is critical in assessing how the probabilities of different scenarios are evolving.
Capital is allocated to each portfolio manager based on an objective evaluation of his individual investment skill. This assessment utilizes a quantitative ranking system which focuses on measures such as demonstrated Sharpe ratio, average annual return to maximum drawdown, liquidity, and correlation to market beta and correlation among portfolio managers. Macro investment ideas are expressed through directional, non-directional and extension strategies across our opportunity set.
Risk management is fully integrated into the investment process. The daily risk management process is designed to ensure that the portfolio's aggregate risk profile is consistent with its return objective and risk tolerance. There is an emphasis on minimizing drawdown by limiting concentration and correlation risk, which is achieved by clearly identifying and measuring factor sensitivities across the portfolio. The risk monitoring process evaluates pre- and post-trade positioning across multiple dimensions, including aggregate interest rate, credit, and currency sensitivities, ex-ante value at risk (VaR), sensitivity to macro factors, as well as through a spectrum of historical scenarios and stress tests.

results.name: Covalis Capital Master Fund
results.management_company_description:
Covalis Capital is multi-sector specialist that focuses primarily on equities of Utilities, Infrastructure, Real Estate, Autos Value Chain, Industrials, Materials, Energy, Telecommunication and Renewables sectors globally.

Founded in 2012, Covalis manages $2.8bn in capital across both private and public equities, spanning low net hedge fund products, directional strategies and co-investments.

While the business started in 2012, the core Covalis team has been successfully managing capital with a consistent investment philosophy since 2004. Prior to founding the business, Zach Mecelis, CIO, and Peter Murphy, Head of Research, ran a hedge fund strategy at Nobel Group and prior to that, were running a strategy at GLG Partners.

At the core, the investment philosophy is based on ensuring deep sector specialism and a rigorous proprietary research approach. The investment team is comprised of over 50 Investment Professionals organized by sector focus. That said, the team operates on an integrated basis with strong collaboration, ensuring we extract valuable research synergies that are becoming more relevant as the energy transition is increasing the interconnections amongst our core sectors.

Our hedge fund products are focused on equity long short investment. Stylistically, the approach is relative value, where we seek to implement ideas hedged at the trade level within sectors, and we are agnostic between long and short alpha. At the over all fund level this leads to a tight factor exposure and uncorrelated profile.
results.strategy_description: The Covalis Capital Master Fund Limited (the “Fund”) follows an equity focused long short strategy. The team’s fundamental research approach is centered on developing a clear variant perception in our investments, and identifying catalysts that will unlock value. In terms of asset class exposure, over 80% of risk is expressed through equities, with the residual being in fixed income and commodities. In addition, the Fund has the ability to invest up to 15% in privates. The implementation of the equity book is relative value, with sub-sector hedging at the idea level, that results in a low market exposure of ± 15% and constrained factor risk.

The Covalis Capital Partners Master Fund Limited (the “Fund”) employs a long-short, low-net strategy, focused primarily on equities of Utilities, Infrastructure, Real Estate, Autos Value Chain, Industrials, Materials, Energy, Telecommunication and Renewables sectors mainly in developed OECD countries. The securities traded by the Fund are typically mid or large cap companies, and hence the Fund is highly liquid. The core investable universe consists of c. 800 companies globally in which the team is active at any given time. We follow a deep dive fundamental research approach supported by a large team of analysts. Each analyst is generally responsible for coverage of 15-30 companies, enabling Covalis’ competitive advantage via its research focus and dedication to several related industries.

The Fund follows a relative value investment approach and therefore seeks to hedge at the idea level within sectors. We are agnostic between long and short ideas, but have a strong preference for avoiding using index products to hedge. Actively trading around catalysts is critical to ensuring we optimize risk reward and drives the turnover in the strategy. The Fund also utilizes European sovereign fixed income instruments opportunistically to hedge country risk.

At the Fund level, we typically run a tight factor risk profile with idiosyncratic risk explaining over 75% of our volatility. We look to constrain beta exposure and sector tilts to 15% of NAV and generally run significantly tighter.

results.management_company_description: Modular Asset Management (Singapore) Pte. Ltd. (the “Firm”) was incorporated in March 2019 by Mr. Jimmy Lim (CEO/CIO) and Mr. Matthew Cannon (COO/CRO) to enable the spin-out of Mr. Lim’s team from Millennium and facilitate the launch of the Modular Asian Macro Master Fund on January 2020.
results.strategy_description:
The Master Fund’s investment philosophy is founded on a belief in the value of specialization and decentralization. The Investment Manager believes that geographical and product specialization provides a persistent competitive advantage. Domain expertise allows a deeper understanding of idiosyncratic, geographical and product level market drivers. Based on this, the Investment Manager seeks to repeatedly extract risk premia from individual markets. Aggregating the modules’ return streams, which have historically exhibited low correlation amongst themselves, the Master Fund aims to achieve persistent steady returns with a high Sharpe Ratio. The investment philosophy permeates through the organizational structure of the Master Fund, the investment style and the nature of return streams.
The Investment Manager’s centralized research function supports individual modules with bottom-up analysis and works together with the CIO team to identify, predict and monetize top-down thematic trends. In doing so, the research team deploys a range of primarily quantitative tools, ranging from short-term tactical allocation models to long-term fundamental economic analysis.
The Master Fund will focus a significant majority of trades and investments in the Asia-Pacific region. Having already surpassed the US and Euro area as the largest economic region globally, the Investment Manager expects Asia-Pacific to grow at a significantly higher rate than major developed economies. Within the region, countries exhibit significantly different levels of economic and financial market development. Accordingly, the return streams available from different countries differ in magnitude and nature. The Investment Manager believes that market growth will provide ongoing opportunities to extract alpha.
Although the Master Fund’s portfolio will consist primarily of the strategies mentioned above, the Master Fund may also take positions in a wide range of asset classes, financial instruments and strategies, which may not clearly fall within those mentioned above, but which the Investment Manager believes are consistent with the Master Fund’s investment objective.

results.name: PAG Capital Structure Opportunity Fund
results.strategy_description: PAG Capital Structure Opportunity strategy ("CSO") is a Corporate Multi-Strategy Fund which focuses on inefficiencies in the Asian convertible bond universe and related corporate securities across a number of non-correlated strategies. The core strategy allocation traverses the range of opportunities presented by equity-linked products across the cycle including directional equity, stressed/distressed credit and volatility/arbitrage. The team also allocates capital to take advantage of event-driven or market-driven dislocations on an opportunistic basis in asset classes that complement the core exposures; these opportunities have included GDRs, blocks, HY bonds, and traditional ECM. CSO focuses on capital preservation through structuring, hedging and capital re-allocation, incorporating multiple portfolio-level stress scenarios and liquidity shocks to drive overlay macro hedges, with a conservative leverage of 2x to 2.5x. The strategy is managed by Chris Arcoumanis, who joined PAG in November 2018 after starting his career at Lehman Brothers and spending 10 years at Nomura Principal Investments/BFAM Partners where he was a Partner and led the Equity-Linked Business.

results.name: Amundi Chenavari Credit Fund
results.management_company_description:
Chenavari is an established, credit-focused asset manager with a core expertise in European markets. With expertise across the liquidity spectrum of credit, Chenavari aims to profit from idiosyncrasies and inefficiencies within credit markets, which are due to macro (such as banks' deleveraging, monetary policies, etc.) as well as technical factors. The Firm concentrates its investment activity on fundamental strategies that may offer attractive risk-reward profiles on a relative value basis with low market correlation and low beta to broad credit markets.

Chenavari’s investment strategies can be segmented across three groups: 

•	Liquid strategies, including investments in single name corporates, European financials, credit indices, asset-backed securities, across both cash and derivative markets;
•	Private Credit strategies, such as portfolio acquisitions of primarily performing loans; risk sharing/significant risk transfer, asset-based lending, and specialty finance (new loan origination) in consumer finance, receivables and leasing; and
•	CLO management, including investment in senior secured loans and revolving credit facilities through European collateralised loan obligation structures.
results.strategy_description: The Strategy is a European focused fundamental long/short credit strategy with a dynamic allocation to Chenavari’s two sub-strategies: Long/Short Corporate Credit (40-50% allocation) and Long/Short European Financials (40-50% allocation). The Strategy targets investments in the European credit market, from opportunities which arise from inefficiencies and dislocations driven by a combination of Central Bank actions, continuing bank deleveraging, corporate fundamentals and geopolitical uncertainty. Within the L/S European Corporate sub-strategy, the Fund intends to capture alpha through fundamental and technical analysis. The strategy aims at identifying any mispricing or misunderstood credit situations across Europe. This strategy is therefore long/short; shorts can be implemented via repos, total return swaps and credit default swaps (“CDS”). The strategy invests in corporate bonds with a minimum rating of B-, with no private placements or illiquid issues. Within the L/S European Financials sub-strategy, the Fund invests primarily in bonds such as Senior Non-Preferred, legacy Tier 1, Tier 2, Contingent Convertible AT1 bonds (“CoCos”), as well as CDS. Investments are also diversified across duration, geography and issuer typology (universal bank, investment bank, insurance company etc.). To enable an active trading approach, the strategy focuses on more liquid instruments and aims at limiting investments in AT1 bonds to a net exposure of a maximum of 15% of the Fund. The Investment Process uses a fundamental, research-driven approach, with a focus on alpha opportunities and low correlation to the main asset classes. Trade implementation is made across the instruments perceived to offer the best value (both cash and derivatives).

results.strategy_description:
Chenavari CORE Opportunities Fund (the “Fund”) is an open-ended commingled investment-vehicle with a liquidity profile suited to take advantage of the opportunities arising in European credit markets. The Fund seeks to find value in opportunistic liquid credit investments offering strong fundamental value and/or structural protection such as European ABS, CLOs or European Bank bonds and in opportunistic Short-Term Private Asset-Backed transactions. 

The Fund remains well positioned in the current market environment as regulatory capital pressure continues to affect European banks whose deleveraging and capital optimisation requirements contribute to a favourable environment for opportunistic credit investing across the liquidity spectrum. Secondly, we believe that the Fund is well-suited to target opportunities arising in European credit markets which have traditionally been more resilient in the inflation/rate increase cycle than their U.S. counterparts. The Fund’s dynamic overlay seeks to contain market volatility and low correlation to overall markets.

Overall, the Fund is predominantly an asset-backed credit portfolio exhibiting a risk-adjusted yield to a market environment influenced by broader geopolitical influences and heightened asset volatility from tightening policy. This dynamic approach to investment strategy allows the Fund to generate steady theta and low correlation to overall markets.

The firm has offices in London and New York; its investment team of 40+ professionals are based out of the London headquarters.
results.strategy_description:
The Fulcrum Horizon Fund aims to capture alpha from a diversified portfolio of equities across sectors and regions, focused on second and third order effects of long-term sector trends and tactical around short-term events. It is a highly differentiated, fundamental portfolio, with 75% of alpha generated from the short side, minimal stock-specific risk. results.management_company_description:
Contingency Capital invests in legal assets: we finance illiquid assets where the primary driver for unlocking the asset’s value is related to a legal, tax, or regulatory process. This includes loans to law firms, buying and financing claims, financing portfolios of litigation claims, and investing in other special situations assets that are uncorrelated to the public equity and debt markets. Unlike other litigation funders, we look at a broader scope of investments and take a credit-oriented approach. We try to structure our investments to have seniority, floating interest rates, and downside and duration protection.

Our first fund, Contingency Capital Fund I launched in June 2021 and had its final close in December 2022. It is approximately 60% deployed and we expect to be fully invested during the second half of 2024. The investments in Fund I have generated a cash-on cash return of 13% over their life and are generally uncorrelated to the broader credit and equity markets. We are targeting a first close for Fund II in the second quarter of 2024.

The fund manager, Contingency Capital LLC, was founded by Brandon Baer, who has over 20 years of experience investing in legal assets at D. E. Shaw and Fortress before founding Contingency Capital in late 2020. In addition to Fund I, Contingency Capital manages a fund of one targeting both high and lower yield opportunities of shorter duration. As of September 30, 2023, Contingency Capital has approximately $690 million of AUM. results.name: System 2 Master Fund
results.management_company_description:
The fund invests in convertible and capital structure relative value opportunities, primarily in Europe.

System 2 uses a core group of nine relative value transaction types to exploit mis-pricings of securities in the same capital structure. They identify the optimal mix of transaction types at any one point in time to construct a portfolio that is “long the wings”, net flat to credit, net flat to equity, with positive carry System 2’s core relative value transaction types are: (i) long senior / short junior, (ii) long junior / short senior, (iii) credit vs options, (iv) synthetic calls, (v) synthetic puts, (vi) long volatility, (vii) long / short pari credit, (viii) event linked credit, and (ix) short credit System 2 uses quantitative methods to filter the universe of possible trades in each transaction type, then undertakes a fundamental and legal review of those trades that present the greatest asymmetry. Provided the fundamental and legal review supports a conversion thesis / does not reveal anything that would interfere with conversion or make the mispricing endure for longer than anticipated, the trade proceeds to the portfolio. 

The market hedges - including credit market, equity market, interest rates, FX and volatility - isolate exposure to the mis-priced pairs of securities in the same capital structure, insulating the portfolio from key market risks. 

When we find a compelling anomaly, we seek similar anomalies that might indicate a larger investment theme justifying further research and investment.

At System 2, we believe that human bias can put even sound investments at risk. To guard against the impact of emotions, human biases and changing circumstances, we use processes, including our risk management processes and checklists.

Investment Process: The investment process employed by the System 2 investment team utilizes four phases with respect to the flow of an investment idea from inception to trade execution as follows: (1) sourcing; (2) evaluation; (3) decision process; and (4) portfolio management. Risk is considered at every stage of this process, from capital allocation to security selection, hedge sizing, and performance review. Risk oversight permeates portfolio construction and results in the production of meaningful risk metrics that are consistent with how the portfolio manager views risk.

results.strategy_description:
Palmerston Convertible Arb Master Fund (“PCA”) is a Cayman master/feeder absolute return fund implementing a convertible arbitrage strategy focused primarily on the EMEA and APAC regions. PCA is an all-weather, cycle‑resilient strategy that combines the identification of mispriced volatility with selective credit opportunities to build a consistently convex, uncorrelated, low‑beta portfolio designed to generate alpha across market conditions.  The Fund is differentiated by the portfolio manager’s experience across multiple convert cycles coupled with the firm’s strong credit underwriting. Additionally, the fund’s dynamic portfolio rotation of strategies exploits opportunities across all convertibles markets and conditions. 



The Fund’s investment approach is driven by both quantitative analysis and fundamental credit analysis. Emphasis is placed on the portfolio’s construction as we look to optimize convexity through a balance of trade types. PCA constructs convex risk profiles while hedging out the related equity and interest rate risk, with active rebalancing / gamma trading. Palmerston leverages its fundamental credit analysis skill set and highly experienced team of analysts to manage credit risk in European and Asian Investment Grade and High Yield issuers. The portfolio is diversified, dynamically employing a range of strategies with the core volatility trading augmented with put trades that provide downside protection to equity selloffs, ratchet/special situation trades that provide attractive returns during corporate activity and more credit intensive trades in busted converts and HY issuers. 



PCA identifies the most convex opportunities in the asset class combined with a strong risk management framework encompassing portfolio liquidity, downside risk assessment and trade management to generate attractive risk adjusted returns over a long-term investment horizon with an emphasis on capital preservation.

results.strategy_description:
The Palmerston Credit Master Fund is a Cayman master/feeder absolute return fund implementing a European long/short credit strategy across the debt capital structure. The fund targets 10-12% returns with 5% volatility through the cycle, by focusing on convexity through a mix of deep dive fundamental research and instrument selection. The Fund's investment approach is driven primarily by strong fundamental credit analysis, and augmented by research into macro and regulatory drivers, as well as specific security documentation to assess the optimum medium in which risk is taken. The fund targets investment opportunities in both European financials and corporates with capital allocated dynamically between the two. The strong fundamental approach places emphasis on underlying credit trends, but risk positions also focus on potential event risk and changes in capital structure.

The portfolio consists primarily of cash securities, both long and short, with CDS contracts representing a small level of total investments. The fund has relatively concentrated positions with around 60/70 strategies typically employed, with individual name concentration and jump-to-default risk restricted by rigorous risk approach. Given the strong fundamental approach, trade time horizons are reasonably long, typically 4-6 months, with some positions being retained for longer. As such the portfolio turnover is typically around 1.5 times per year. Credit analysis is the dominant trade driver, but investments are also driven by event risk, relative value and specific instrument documentation. The fund has a rigorous investment process, with each strategy sized by conviction, convexity, anticipated volatility, market timing and limit framework. All positions are supported by a detailed write-up incorporating the reasoning for the trade, targets and loss management parameters, which all trades are then monitored against. 

Fund leverage is relatively low, and limited to a maximum of 300% on a gross basis, while net leverage is modest and cannot be more than 125%. Portfolio construction is designed to limit volatility with a focus on lower beta assets as long positions and higher beta assets as shorts, utilising the convexity of the underlying instruments. Additionally investments focus on market liquidity to ensure they can be traded in periods of market disruption. Risk is managed according to proportional shifts in the underlying credit spread, rather than credit ratings, which ensures leverage is reduced in periods of high volatility. The manager can take directional bets within the portfolio risk and leverage limits but the key investment driver is individual credit performance.

results.management_company_description:
Silver Point Capital, L.P. (“Silver Point”, the “Firm”, "we") was founded in 2002 by Edward Mulé and Robert O’Shea, both previously partners at Goldman Sachs (“Goldman”), where together they built and co-headed numerous global credit businesses for the firm. 

Upon departing from Goldman, Mr. Mulé and Mr. O’Shea partnered to establish Silver Point in 2002 to replicate the credit businesses that they had built and managed while at Goldman. The Founders’ vision for Silver Point was to build a world-class private investment firm that would specialize in investing in credit and special situations opportunities.  They believed that they could leverage their experience and expertise to build a global credit investing business that would seek to generate attractive risk-adjusted returns across credit cycles for its investors.

Today, the Firm manages approximately $45 billion in investable assets across synergistic credit strategies, comprising (1) opportunistic credit and special situations funds, which include an evergreen global special situations investing strategy focused on publicly traded credit markets (the “Flagship Hedge Funds”) managing $13 billion in investable assets, (2) a dislocation drawdown strategy (the “Dislocation Drawdown Funds”) managing $7 billion in investable assets,  (3) a performing middle market lending strategy (our “Direct Lending Strategy”) managing $17 billion in investable assets; and (4) a liquid performing credit business managing approximately $8 billion.
results.strategy_description:
Distressed Opportunity Institutional Partners II (the “Fund”) seeks to achieve superior risk-adjusted returns by investing opportunistically in debt, equity and other financial obligations and assets, with a particular focus on companies and/or instruments that are mispriced, stressed, distressed, overleveraged and/or going through restructurings, bankruptcies or other complex situations in which the Fund can play an active role in driving events. The longer-locked structure will allow us to maximize value by (i) being more concentrated in highly attractive process-oriented investments; and (ii) capitalizing on illiquid investments that offer attractive absolute and risk-adjusted returns.

The Fund seeks to capitalize on market inefficiencies that arise in the credit markets due to (i) forced sell-offs and dislocations that result from market re-pricings; (ii) process complexities; (iii) the opacity of stressed, distressed, or bankrupt businesses; and (iv) the resource intensity required to navigate complicated capital structures, creditor laws, and credit documentation. As a large and experienced credit manager with a 22+ year track record in the strategy, Silver Point is well positioned to take advantage of the opportunities that persist during and following a market dislocation. This opportunity set includes both the initial liquid, stressed opportunity that arises from a market disruption, as well as the event-driven, complex distressed and turnaround opportunities that we drive given our experienced team, depth of resources, and expertise in the space.
       
Please note we are open to discussion around strategic partnerships at certain size minimums. Additionally, Silver Point offers both offshore and onshore fund offerings for investors.
results.region_exposure_description: The Funds have a global mandate. While Silver Point has experience pursuing investment and restructuring processes in over 50 jurisdictions globally, the majority of the portfolio tends to be in North America, given North America has the largest leveraged credit markets and the strongest debtor / creditor laws. We also have significant exposure to Western Europe and have historically had exposure to other regions including Europe, Asia, South America and others. The strength of creditor laws, process risks, and jurisdictional risks will all impact both risk adjusted and relative returns and will be taken into account when evaluating positions. Ultimately, the geographic breakdown of the Fund will be purely opportunistic and will leverage our experience and expertise in global distressed investing.

results.portfolio_additional_details:
The Funds will invest in both middle market and large companies opportunistically across geographies and industries, assessing the best risk adjusted as well as relative value investments. The Funds’ portfolios will likely be primarily invested in (i) senior secured debt, or in unsecured debt with secured debt characteristics purchased through distressed and liquidation trades; (ii) loans and securities of companies undergoing bankruptcy or other in or out of court restructurings; (iii) dislocated credit trading at prices below what we believe to be its fundamental value; (iv) rescue financings; (v) distressed loan portfolios; (vi) distressed real estate; (vii) opportunistic stressed / event-driven loans and securities; (viii) post-restructured equity positions, typically in names where we have taken an active role in driving the restructuring process and anticipate taking an active role in further unlocking value at the company post-restructuring; as well as (ix) illiquid stressed or distressed investments with attractive returns.

We believe that being active in an investment often increases return, shortens duration, and decreases risk. DOIP II is a long-only, unlevered strategy and anticipates investing in 40-60 meaningful positions with a maximum position sizing at 20% of aggregate commitments.

This range has been consistent across our lending funds, since the launch of SCF I in 2015.

Where possible, Parkman seeks to minimize risk by investing in products and technologies that are sufficiently mature that a reasonable judgement about their commercial prospects can be made. Parkman generally seeks to avoid binary clinical events given their broadly unattractive risk-reward and their inherent lack of predictability. We participate in binary events on a selective basis and maintain a diversified portfolio that is balanced across all subsectors of healthcare.
